items.raw_excerpt: It’s not a public holiday, Constitution Day or the King's birthday, but Denmark’s flag is flown every September 5th from public buildings and buses across the country.
items.summary_en: Every September 5th, Denmark flies its flag from public buildings and buses. The day marks Flag Day, when the country honours its military and those who have served abroad. It is not a public holiday, but it has become a tradition across the nation.

items.title_en: Why Denmark Flies Its Flag on September 5th

items.title_original: Flag Day: Why does Denmark commemorate its military on September 5th?

items.raw_excerpt: Melissa Johns, 36, from Greater Manchester, says two weeks paternity leave is 'not enough' in 2026.
items.summary_en: Families in England say two weeks of paternity leave is not enough for new fathers. Melissa Johns, 36, from Greater Manchester, says dads need more time at home after a baby is born. The debate is growing in 2026 over how to better support new parents.

items.raw_excerpt: Three final-quarter goals from young forward Emma McDonald inspired the Western Bulldogs to a soaring 27-point win over Sydney.

items.summary_en: Malaysian state Sarawak has been badly hit by transboundary haze from forest fires in Indonesia. Local people and businesses are struggling with the poor air quality. The haze is the worst the region has experienced since 2019.

items.raw_excerpt: Among the international collection of sculptures lining the N249, one figure commands a different kind of attention: the statue of Dr Gregório Rafael da Silva de Almeida.
items.summary_en: A statue of Dr Gregório Rafael da Silva de Almeida stands along the N249 road in Sintra, Portugal. He was a beloved local doctor who treated everyone regardless of their ability to pay. The statue is part of a collection of roadside sculptures, but it stands out as a tribute to a real community hero.
